title: Charism Assessment
description: A prayerful, introductory look at the gifts the Holy Spirit may be developing in you for service to God and others.
answerPrompt: Choose how true this is of you as you actually are.

questions.text: I naturally enjoy organizing people, tasks, or resources so that a goal can be accomplished smoothly.
When something is disorganized, I can usually see what needs to be arranged or coordinated.
I often find myself taking responsibility for planning schedules, tasks, events, or practical details.
People have recognized that I am good at bringing order and structure to situations.
My organization and coordination often help a group accomplish more effectively what it set out to do.
I feel fulfilled when I can turn a complicated plan into something clear, organized, and workable.
When involved in a group or ministry, I naturally notice the practical details that need to be coordinated for things to work well.
I feel drawn to take responsibility when a group needs direction.
I can usually identify a clear direction or goal when others are uncertain about what to do.
I often find myself stepping forward to guide, coordinate, or motivate others.
People naturally look to me when a decision needs to be made or a group needs direction.
My leadership tends to help people work together toward a shared purpose.
I experience a sense of purpose when I can help others move toward a meaningful goal.
In difficult situations, I am willing to take responsibility rather than wait for someone else to lead.
I enjoy creating, building, repairing, or improving something tangible.
I can often figure out how to make or fix something through practical skill and experimentation.
I frequently find myself working with tools, materials, technology, design, or practical projects.
Others have recognized my ability to make, repair, or improve things.
The things I create or improve are useful and contribute meaningfully to the needs of others.
I feel deeply satisfied when I can use practical skills to produce something good and useful.
When something needs to be made, repaired, designed, or practically solved, I am often one of the people others turn to.
I feel naturally drawn to express ideas, faith, or emotions through creative forms.
I often see possibilities, connections, or ideas that others may not immediately notice.
Creative expression such as art, music, writing, storytelling, design, or other forms of expression regularly appears in my life.
Others have noticed or appreciated my creativity or ability to express ideas in an engaging way.
My creative expression helps others understand, experience, or appreciate something in a meaningful way.
I feel energized and fulfilled when I have an opportunity to create or express something.
When I need to communicate something important, I often think of a creative or memorable way to express it.
I genuinely enjoy helping others understand something they previously found difficult.
I can usually explain an idea in a way that makes sense to the person listening.
I frequently find myself explaining, demonstrating, instructing, or helping others learn.
People have told me that I explain things clearly or that they understand something better after I have explained it.
My explanations often help people grow in understanding and apply what they have learned.
I feel fulfilled when I see someone understand or master something because I helped them learn it.
When someone asks me about a subject I know, I naturally want to help them understand it rather than simply give them an answer.
I have a strong desire to learn and understand how things work, especially in matters that can help others.
I am often able to gather, remember, connect, or understand information that is useful for solving problems.
I regularly spend time reading, researching, studying, or learning beyond what is immediately required of me.
People sometimes come to me because they believe I know or can find information they need.
What I learn often becomes useful in helping others make better decisions or understand situations.
I experience genuine satisfaction from discovering and understanding new information.
When faced with an unfamiliar problem, my instinct is often to investigate and learn more before deciding what to do.
I am drawn to help people understand what would be wise or appropriate in difficult situations.
I can often see the deeper principles or practical implications behind a situation.
People regularly seek my perspective when they are facing important or complicated decisions.
Others have told me that my advice helped them see a situation more clearly.
My advice tends to help people make decisions that lead toward what is good, responsible, and life-giving.
I feel fulfilled when I can help someone apply truth wisely to a real-life situation.
When someone brings me a difficult problem, I naturally try to understand both the situation and what would be the best course of action.
I have a strong desire to recognize what is truly good, trustworthy, or spiritually significant in a situation.
I can often sense when something is not quite right even when I cannot immediately explain why.
I frequently pay attention to the motives, influences, or deeper dynamics behind what is happening.
Others have asked me to help them determine whether a situation, decision, or influence is trustworthy.
My discernment has helped people avoid confusion, unhealthy influences, or poor decisions.
I find it fulfilling to help distinguish what is genuinely helpful from what only appears to be good.
When making an important decision, I naturally look beyond appearances and consider what may be influencing the situation underneath.
I feel a strong desire to speak truth when I believe something important needs to be addressed.
I can sometimes recognize a truth or concern that others have overlooked.
I regularly find myself speaking honestly about matters of faith, justice, values, or what I believe is right.
Others have told me that something I said challenged them, encouraged them to change, or helped them see something differently.
When I speak difficult truths with love, it can lead people or communities toward greater faithfulness.
I feel a deep sense of responsibility when I believe an important truth should be expressed rather than left unspoken.
When I see something that conflicts with God's truth or deeply held values, I find it difficult simply to remain silent.
I naturally trust God even when circumstances give me little reason to feel confident.
I am able to encourage others to believe that God can work even when a situation appears difficult or impossible.
In challenging situations, I frequently respond by placing my trust in God's providence.
Others have recognized in me a strong confidence in God, especially during difficult circumstances.
My faith and trust in God often strengthen the faith of people around me.
I experience deep peace or fulfillment when I place difficult situations completely in God's hands.
When others become discouraged about what seems impossible, I naturally remind them of God's power and faithfulness.
I feel a strong desire to pray specifically and persistently for other people and their needs.
I can remain faithful in prayer even when I do not immediately see results.
I regularly find myself remembering particular people, families, situations, or intentions in prayer.
Others have noticed that I pray consistently for them or have asked me to pray for a particular intention.
My prayer often brings spiritual support, peace, or encouragement to people and situations I pray for.
I experience deep fulfillment when I spend time praying for others.
When I hear about someone's struggle or need, one of my first responses is often to pray for that person.
I feel deeply drawn to bring comfort, restoration, and healing to people who are suffering.
I am often able to respond sensitively to people who are experiencing emotional, physical, or spiritual pain.
I regularly find myself caring for people who are hurting or helping them move toward healing.
People have experienced my presence, prayer, encouragement, or care as something that helped them heal or recover.
My involvement with hurting people tends to bring comfort, hope, restoration, or renewed strength.
I feel a deep sense of fulfillment when I can help someone who is suffering experience healing or renewed hope.
When I encounter someone who is hurting, my natural response is to want to do something that could bring them relief or restoration.
I have a deep desire to grow in love and devotion toward God.
I naturally turn to prayer, worship, Scripture, or the sacraments as expressions of my relationship with God.
I regularly seek ways to deepen my personal relationship with God through spiritual practices.
Others can recognize that my faith is expressed not only in what I believe but also in how I live and relate to God.
My devotion to God influences the way I treat people, make decisions, and live my daily life.
I experience deep joy and fulfillment through prayer, worship, and growing closer to God.
Even in ordinary daily activities, I naturally look for ways to remain aware of God's presence and respond to Him with love.
I genuinely enjoy helping others with practical needs without needing recognition.
I am usually able to notice what needs to be done and quietly take care of it.
I frequently help with practical tasks, behind-the-scenes work, or whatever is needed to support others.
People often describe me as dependable and willing to help when something needs to be done.
My practical help makes it easier for other people to carry out their responsibilities or ministry.
I feel fulfilled when I know that my practical contribution has made someone else's work or life easier.
In a group setting, I often notice tasks that others have overlooked and step in to help.
I genuinely enjoy welcoming people and helping them feel comfortable and included.
I can usually sense what would help a guest or newcomer feel more at ease.
I frequently make an effort to welcome, include, host, or care for people who are new or unfamiliar.
People have told me that they feel comfortable, accepted, or at home when they are with me.
My hospitality helps people feel that they belong and are valued.
I feel particularly fulfilled when I can create a warm and welcoming environment for others.
When someone enters a group where they do not know many people, I naturally notice them and try to help them feel included.
I naturally want to strengthen people who are discouraged, struggling, or uncertain.
I can often recognize what someone needs to hear to regain courage or hope.
I regularly encourage, affirm, motivate, or comfort people around me.
People often come to me when they need reassurance, motivation, or emotional support.
My words or presence often help people regain confidence, hope, or strength.
I feel deeply fulfilled when I see someone become stronger because of encouragement I gave them.
When someone is struggling or doubting themselves, my instinct is usually to look for a way to strengthen them.
I feel a strong desire to help people encounter Jesus and grow in faith.
I am comfortable finding ways to speak about faith with people who may not share my beliefs.
I regularly look for opportunities to share the Gospel, invite others into faith, or participate in missionary activities.
Others recognize me as someone who naturally reaches out to people and invites them toward faith or community.
My efforts to share faith help people become more open to God, the Church, or a deeper spiritual life.
I experience joy and fulfillment when I see someone take a step closer to Christ because of an invitation or witness I offered.
When I meet someone who is distant from faith, I naturally wonder how I might help them encounter God.
I feel naturally moved to give generously when I see a genuine need.
I am able to give my resources freely without constantly worrying about what I will have left.
I regularly give money, possessions, time, or other resources to support people, ministries, or worthy causes.
Others have recognized me as someone who is generous or willing to share what I have.
My generosity has enabled people, families, or ministries to do things they otherwise might not have been able to do.
I experience genuine joy when I can use what I have to bless someone else.
When I become aware of a meaningful need, my first thought is often about how I could contribute toward meeting it.

scoring.method: sum the seven 0–3 responses per charism (0–21 each, equally weighted); rank all 18 scores highest to lowest; the top three ranks are the strongest indicated charisms, preserving ties

administration.title: Administration
administration.description: Excels at planning, managing people, resources, and/or time; has an innate sense of how an organization can be run efficiently and effectively.

leadership.title: Leadership
leadership.description: Innate ability to create a vision and motivate others to complete it; provides direction and empowers others to use their gifts for the good of the community.

craftsmanship.title: Craftsmanship
craftsmanship.description: Extraordinarily gifted in working with their hands; excels in making tangible things and recognizes that these abilities are used for the glory of God.

creativity.title: Creativity & Expression
creativity.description: Ordinarily artistic in writing, art, music, or other forms; naturally innovative and energized when creative abilities are used in service of God.

teaching.title: Teaching
teaching.description: Conveys Gospel truth in ways others can easily understand and helps people apply faith in practical ways.

knowledge.title: Knowledge
knowledge.description: Learned understanding of the Catholic faith, Scripture, and Church teaching used to serve the Church and her people.

wisdom.title: Wisdom
wisdom.description: Intuitive application of spiritual truth to particular situations; helps discern appropriate answers to problems.

discernment.title: Discernment
discernment.description: Listens to the movement of the Holy Spirit in self and others, accompanies people on their faith journey, and gets to the heart of the matter.

prophecy.title: Prophecy
prophecy.description: Recognizes truth and is willing to defend what has been revealed as God’s truth, urging others toward right relationship with God.

faith.title: Faith
faith.description: An exceptional trust in God’s power, promises, and providence, especially in difficult or seemingly impossible circumstances.

intercession.title: Intercession
intercession.description: Deeply knows that God answers prayer and actively prays on behalf of others.

healing.title: Healing
healing.description: Restores people toward wholeness in spirit, mind, body, or relationships and recognizes oneself as an instrument of God’s healing grace.

piety.title: Piety
piety.description: Respect for things pertaining to God, especially devotion to Christ in the Eucharist, the Blessed Virgin Mary, and active participation in the sacramental life of the Church.

service.title: Service & Helps
service.description: Cheerfully accomplishes practical or necessary tasks in support of others and ministry, often gladly serving behind the scenes without seeking recognition.

hospitality.title: Hospitality
hospitality.description: Makes people feel welcome by seeing Christ in the stranger, fostering belonging, and helping relationships develop.

encouragement.title: Encouragement
encouragement.description: Motivates others toward practical Christian living, strengthens spiritual growth, and encourages trust in God’s providence.

evangelization.title: Evangelization & Mission
evangelization.description: Shares the faith with the purpose of leading others closer to God through meaningful proclamation of the Gospel.

giving.title: Giving
giving.description: Promotes God’s will by generously providing for others, especially through stewardship, care for the poor, and sharing God’s blessings.
